timeline.body:
- Fix IpPrefix function not using ByteRef offset on calculations, leading to wrong bytes being written to the prefix.
- Fixed the CSVTest case, which was also wrong, leading to a "_wrong * wrong = correct_" situation.
-  ~~Added` a BytesRef randomizer and applied it to the IpPrefixTests suppliers~~
    - ~~This highlighted another bug, which was fixed too~~
    - (Moved to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/109207)

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/109198

timeline.body:
This chain is starting to (And will) get longer over time I think. Should we replace it with a "recommendedModifiers()"? Specially for average cases where all of them are applied.
Maybe not for this PR though, as this is a fix

Wasn't sure about pushing this in this PR, but as it discovered another bug, well...

My idea would be to propagate it to other tests (Or at least to new functions)

reply.body:
:+1: on separating it it for now.

I wonder if we could merge this into `TypedData`'s constructor. It already has a funny hack for `UNSIGNED_LONG`. I wonder if we can do a hack for `BytesRef` and randomize the offset there.
Ok! Extracting to another branch, and merging

About the TypedData constructor, I would avoid it, as I could imagine some test manually adding offsets themselves for some usecase (?)
Not sure, but I feel like there's more control this way

timeline.author: Iván Cea Fontenla

timeline.body: Oh good catch. Lots of  `BytesRef`s do indeed start at 0, but the ones we use might not.
While you are here you could randomly add trailing bytes too. You could fill them with random garbage too if you were especially adventurous.
I think we should merge this one as is and then iterate on the trick to randomize the offsets in the bytesrefs in a follow up chagne.
